blocks.text: Reachability follows links transitively

Model each service as a vertex and each followable communication link as an edge. T is reachable from S if T = S or there is a sequence S → … → T of zero or more legal links. A traversal starts at S, expands linked services, and uses visited state so a cycle does not cause repeated processing.

Alphabetically sorting service names or binary-searching a known name can find a record, but neither operation proves that a communication path connects S to T. BFS and DFS are implementation choices after the graph structure is recognized.

blocks.text: Equal-cost edges turn ride count into BFS depth

BFS starts with A at distance 0, then processes all stations one ride away, then two rides away, and so on. Because every direct ride adds exactly one to the distance, the first time B is discovered its layer number is the minimum possible ride count.

DFS can discover a longer route before a shorter one. A matrix versus a list is a representation decision, and the map is not promised to be a tree. None of those claims establishes minimum edge count.

blocks.text: The output must satisfy every directed precedence edge

Model prerequisite p for task t as p → t. A legal output is a topological order: for every such edge, p appears before t. Indegree processing repeatedly removes tasks with no remaining prerequisites; DFS postorder is another implementation when it also detects cycles.
An ordinary BFS or DFS order may visit every task yet still place t before prerequisite p. Dropping direction erases the meaning of the constraint, and no ordering can satisfy a directed cycle.

blocks.text: A possible graph model is not necessarily a useful one

For each value x in scan order, the maximum sum of a contiguous subarray ending at x is either x alone or the previous ending sum plus x. The update `ending = max(x, ending + x)` retains exactly that decision, while a separate maximum records the best ending seen.

Turning adjacent indices into path edges is mathematically possible, but BFS over that path does not compute the accumulation invariant. An adjacency matrix adds irrelevant pair storage, and calling the sequence a tree does not expose the maximum-sum decision.
Choose graph traversal only when connectivity or repeatable state transitions drive the requested output, not merely because objects can be drawn as vertices.
